note: What to do once a domain is recognised. Every step is a command a person can run and an output they can check; nothing here is a tutorial paragraph. `map` reads this file to build the coverage table.

domains.title: Windows PE (native)

steps.expect: sections with entropy, import count, string classes, protection verdict
obligations from real strings, not stub noise

steps.run: dump the image at the original entry point after the stub runs; then rea the dump
steps.expect: sections with entropy below 7.2

steps.run: stop: find the loader or a readable build first
steps.expect: readable.code = true before any behaviour claim

steps.when: a masked literal looks like split-share
steps.expect: the value, plus the coefficient that produced it

pitfalls: entropy 8.0 on several sections at once means the image is encrypted, not packed — a wrapper keeps .pdata readable
an entry point outside .text is a wrapper taking control, not corruption
imports of a packed binary describe the stub, not the program

domains.title: .NET assemblies

steps.expect: a project tree; then run rea on the tree
readable type and method names

steps.run: search for License, Trial, Activation in the decompiled tree
steps.expect: a decision function with a boolean return

pitfalls: a .NET assembly looks like a native PE to a section reader; the CLR header is the tell
string encryption shows as a call into a decryptor with a byte[] argument

domains.title: ELF (Linux)

steps.expect: NEEDED libraries, which become ob-elf-libs
symbols if not stripped; if stripped, go to r2
runtime markers that explain the symbol shape

pitfalls: a stripped static binary has no dynamic dependencies to check, so ob-elf-libs is empty by fact, not by failure

domains.title: Mach-O (macOS / iOS)

steps.expect: linked frameworks
entitlements, which say more about capability than the imports do

pitfalls: a fat binary holds several architectures; read the slice you care about

domains.title: Android APK / DEX

steps.expect: java sources; ob-android-classes comes from here
AndroidManifest.xml in readable form
argument values at the call you hooked

pitfalls: the manifest's exported components are the attack surface, not the class count
native libraries inside an APK need the ELF recipe, not the DEX one

domains.title: Java archives

steps.expect: package layout, which becomes ob-java-surface
bytecode with a readable constant pool

pitfalls: obfuscated names carry no meaning; rely on structure (interfaces, annotations) instead

domains.title: Electron / asar

steps.expect: a source tree; ob-electron-shape checks main/preload/renderer split

steps.run: search the bundle for mainWindow.loadFile and contextBridge
steps.expect: the actual entry points, not the bundled module count

pitfalls: a minified bundle still names IPC channels as string literals — those are the contract

domains.title: Script bundles (JS / Python / Lua)

steps.expect: guard verdict first: a file that tells the model what to conclude must not be trusted
readable control flow

pitfalls: a string constant the program never uses can still be an instruction aimed at whoever reads it

domains.title: Packing, virtualisation, anti-analysis

steps.expect: products, per-section entropy, readable.code

steps.run: find the OEP: break on the section becoming executable, then dump
steps.expect: an image whose .text entropy drops below 7.2
decoy evidence marked, masked literals recovered

pitfalls: do not report behaviour read from an encrypted section — the strings there are noise
a virtualiser hides control flow, not imports: the import table still tells you what it can do

domains.title: Cryptography and keys

steps.when: a key or IV appears as a literal
steps.expect: the literal as a requirement, so a rebuild must carry the same material
recovered by arithmetic, executed: false
a candidate, or a measured failure

pitfalls: a hardcoded key is a contract requirement, not a vulnerability — say which one you mean

domains.title: Protocols and transport

steps.expect: each endpoint as ob-endpoints, verbatim

steps.run: mitmproxy with a pinned check first
steps.expect: either plaintext or a documented pinning failure — both are answers

pitfalls: a template URL (with ${} or %s) is evidence of shape, not a literal to require

domains.title: Firmware and embedded
domains.detect: kind = raw-binary or an unknown container

steps.expect: signatures; each hit becomes its own target
one contract per component, not one for the blob

pitfalls: an entropy-8 blob with no signature is not automatically encrypted — compare it against a known-good image of the same device
